problem.title: Retail demand forecasting
problem.context: A retailer forecasts weekly demand per store and product for 400 stores and 30,000 products. Monday forecasts for the next eight weeks feed replenishment. Till sales arrive nightly; promotions and holidays strongly affect demand. Three data scientists own the pipeline; central IT operates an unchangeable warehouse.

requirements.text: Produce, every week, the forecast per store and product for the next eight weeks, and deliver it to the replenishment system by Monday 06:00.
Run the forecast again for any past week exactly as it was produced.
Try new model ideas and compare them with the production model on past weeks before they replace it.
Asked for the forecast of a week up to two years back, the team produces the same numbers within one working day.
A new model idea that beats the production model on past weeks reaches production within one week, with no manual step except the approval.
When a weekly run fails, the team is told within 15 minutes, and the replenishment system never receives a partial forecast.
A new team member can run the whole pipeline on their own machine within their first week.
Three data scientists, with no data engineers; the data warehouse stays as it is.
The weekly run must fit in the six hours between the nightly load and the Monday deadline.

points.description: A scheduled ML orchestrator uses versioned data to run automated, provisioned training, evaluation, validation, and model-quality testing pipelines, with CI/CD building, testing, and deploying the required pipelines and components. Approved models are precomputed into forecasts or reports for serving, with the ability to redeploy and switch back to a previous model version if needed.

A versioned-data repository supports scheduled automated pipelines for model training, evaluation, validation, and evidence-based hypothesis testing, with environments provisioned automatically. CI/CD builds, tests, and deploys models and supporting components, while scheduled batch serving writes predictions to storage; multiple model versions can run in production concurrently.

Models are built in a development sandbox and periodically triggered on a schedule, then precomputed and delivered as forecasts or reports, with a single model version in production. Deployment relies on scripts rather than CI/CD automation, and the system has no data versioning, automated environment provisioning, or pipeline testing.

A scheduled ML orchestrator uses versioned data and automatically provisioned environments to run CI/CD-built pipelines that select, train, evaluate, validate, and quality-test models. Approved models are precomputed into forecasts or scores for report delivery, with deployment supporting rollback to a previous model version when needed.

A scheduled ML pipeline uses data versioned in the code repository, automatically provisions its environment, and trains and evaluates multiple model variants through evidence-based hypothesis testing. CI/CD builds, tests, and deploys the models and related components, while batch serving periodically writes predictions to storage and supports multiple model versions in production.

A scheduled ML pipeline retrieves versioned data, uses a dedicated model builder for training, evaluation, and validation, and is supported by automated provisioning and system integration tests. CI/CD builds, tests, and deploys the pipeline components; validated models are precomputed into reports for serving, with rollback to a previous model version when needed.

A scheduled ML pipeline uses data versioned in the code repository to train, evaluate, and validate multiple model variants through evidence-based hypothesis testing. CI/CD automatically provisions environments, builds/tests/deploys models and components, and serves predictions in scheduled data batches; if needed, production can roll back to a previous model version.

A scheduled ML orchestrator uses versioned data and automatically provisioned environments to run model-selection, training, evaluation, and validation pipelines. CI/CD builds, integration-tests, and deploys the required pipeline components; predictions are precomputed and delivered as reports, with the option to roll back to a previous model version if needed.

A scheduled ML pipeline uses versioned data to train and evaluate multiple model variants, applying evidence-based hypothesis tests before CI/CD builds, tests, provisions, and deploys the selected model and supporting components. Predictions are precomputed and delivered as reports; if necessary, the system can redeploy and switch back to a previous model version.

A scheduled ML orchestrator provisions environments, retrieves versioned data, and runs model-building components that train and validate multiple model versions. CI/CD builds, tests, and deploys the required pipelines and components with system integration testing; selected models serve batch predictions to storage, with rollback enabling redeployment of a previous version.

A scheduled ML orchestrator provisions environments, retrieves versioned data, and runs a model-building component that trains and evaluates multiple algorithm or parameter variants, with unit tests for pipeline components. CI/CD builds, tests, and deploys the required pipelines and components; selected model outputs are precomputed and delivered as reports, with rollback to a previous model version if needed.

approaches.idea: What if a scheduled orchestrator owns reproducible training, selection, and batch forecast publication?
What if CI/CD and competing model runs accelerate evidence-based model promotion?
What if a small team keeps the workflow in a development tool and scripts?
approaches.dropped_because: Without data versioning, tests, or automated deployment this cannot support exact historical reruns, safe promotion, and the low-manual-step delivery requirement.

approaches.idea: What if a dedicated model-builder component and integration checks keep orchestration lighter while preserving repeatable batch delivery?
approaches.dropped_because: Its component-centered option was folded into E, which combines that modular builder with explicit multi-model evaluation and scheduled batch delivery.

approaches.idea: What if a dedicated model-builder component combines with multiple candidate training and scheduled batch delivery?

trajectory.hypothesis: Scheduled precomputation should meet R1 and C2; versioned data and rollback should support R2; automated model quality testing and deployment should support R3 and Q2.
trajectory.observation: The combination is valid and unattested. Its automated pieces address repeatability and promotion, but the space does not settle atomic publication, alert timing, point-in-time input capture, or runtime within six hours.

trajectory.hypothesis: Scheduled batch forecasts and CI/CD should meet R1 and Q2; concurrent model versions and hypothesis testing should support R3, while repository data versioning supports Q1/R2.
trajectory.observation: The point is valid and unattested. It strongly expresses model comparison, but multiple production versions add operational complexity for three scientists and do not alone specify safe all-or-nothing forecast delivery.

trajectory.hypothesis: A lightweight scheduled development-tool workflow should reduce overhead for C1 and may deliver reports for R1, but it is unlikely to provide exact reruns or safe rapid promotion.
trajectory.observation: The valid but unattested point keeps operational burden low, yet no versioning, tests, or deployment automation leave the most constraining reproducibility, comparison, and promotion needs unsupported. Dropped.

trajectory.hypothesis: Add automated model selection to make the winning backtest candidate explicit, improving R3 and Q2.
trajectory.observation: Model selection strengthens the candidate-to-production path. The point is valid and unattested; a single selected model avoids the complexity of concurrent production versions.

trajectory.hypothesis: Train multiple candidates in the pipeline to support R3 and strengthen selection before promotion.
trajectory.observation: The valid, unattested point makes comparison concrete, though N production versions are not necessary to compare on historical weeks and increase operational burden.

trajectory.hypothesis: Replace the monolithic model-building pipeline with a dedicated builder component and system integration testing, retaining versioned data and scheduled batch output; this may improve Q4 and Q3 while keeping R1/R2 support.
trajectory.observation: The valid, unattested point provides a distinct component-centered option; integration tests address pipeline seams, but the space offers no alerting or atomic-publication decision.

trajectory.hypothesis: Retain model selection, versioned inputs, rollback, and scheduled precomputation as the strongest integrated path for R1-R3 and Q1-Q2.
trajectory.observation: Reuses P4; it remains the best balanced point for selection and rollback. Exact reruns still require immutable snapshots of source data, code, and configuration beyond what the represented choices guarantee.

trajectory.hypothesis: Keep multi-candidate historical evaluation but use rollback to a single active production model, reducing burden while retaining R3 and Q2.
trajectory.observation: The valid, unattested point preserves parallel model exploration while avoiding concurrent production operations. This is a better operational balance than P5.

trajectory.hypothesis: Fold the component-centered member into a new approach that trains several candidates and emits scheduled batch predictions, combining Q4-oriented modularity with R3 comparison.
trajectory.observation: The valid, unattested combination brings multiple candidate training into the dedicated builder and uses batch writes for scheduled output; it retains the integration-test focus.

trajectory.hypothesis: Switch the validation focus from model-quality tests to end-to-end system integration, seeking stronger reliability at system boundaries while retaining automated model selection.
trajectory.observation: The valid, unattested point strengthens system-level integration coverage while preserving selection and rollback; alert timing and atomic publication remain outside the space.

trajectory.hypothesis: Use a dedicated data-version repository and precomputed forecast reports while retaining multi-candidate evaluation, addressing Q1 and R1 without concurrent production models.
trajectory.observation: The valid, unattested point aligns the output more closely with precomputed forecasts and uses a dedicated version repository; model variant comparison remains explicit.

trajectory.hypothesis: Refine the new component-centered approach with precomputed report delivery and component unit tests while retaining candidate comparison and rollback.
trajectory.observation: The valid, unattested refinement keeps the candidate tournament and modular builder, aligns output with precomputed forecasts, and adds component-level unit tests.

adrs.title: Schedule and publish weekly forecasts
adrs.context: The weekly deadline favors precomputed batch output on a schedule. The space offers batch and precompute serving, but does not decide atomic publication, failure alerting within 15 minutes, warehouse integration details, or six-hour capacity.

options.name: Precomputed report delivery
cons: No value specifies atomic handoff or deadline/runtime guarantees.
options.reason: The brief asks for an eight-week forecast delivered on Monday, favoring offline precomputation.

options.name: Scheduled batch writes
pros: Directly writes scheduled prediction batches to storage.
cons: Still leaves completeness and notification mechanics open.
options.reason: A batch output aligns with the warehouse-fed replenishment workflow.

adrs.title: Reproduce historical forecasts and compare candidates
adrs.context: Historical reruns require preserved inputs and candidate comparison requires repeatable training and evaluation. The space covers data-versioning and model-building choices, but does not specify immutable snapshots of source records, code, configuration, or a full backtest protocol.

options.name: Orchestrated selection on versioned data
pros: Checks the quality of trained candidates before selection.
cons: Versioned data alone may not preserve every input and execution detail.
options.reason: Selection in the automated pipeline creates a direct route from backtest to chosen candidate.

options.name: CI/CD candidate tournament
pros: Trains multiple variants and evaluates them with evidence-based hypothesis testing.
cons: Repository-based data versioning and automated candidate handling need careful scale management.
options.reason: This gives model experimentation a first-class path while keeping one active production model.

options.name: Component validation workflow
pros: Encapsulation and integration checks make pipeline behavior easier to run and inspect.
cons: The selected values do not themselves define candidate backtesting or exact historical reconstruction.
options.reason: A dedicated builder and integration checks suit a small team maintaining a modular pipeline.

options.name: No reproducible automation
cons: Cannot support reliable historical reruns or systematic candidate comparison.
options.reason: Dropped because it misses the central reproducibility and model comparison needs.

adrs.title: Promote models and operate environments
adrs.context: The small team needs a low-manual-step release path, rollback, and reproducible local environments. The space covers CI/CD scope, provisioning, and rollback, but does not specify approval gates, monitoring alerts, or atomic forecast output.

options.name: Orchestrated component delivery with rollback
pros: Coordinates components and enables return to a previous model.
cons: An orchestrator can add operational weight for three scientists.
options.reason: Choose when integrated run coordination is worth the added platform responsibility.

options.name: CI/CD with model rollback
pros: Automates model build and deployment while retaining rollback.
cons: The team must define an approval gate and operational controls.
options.reason: Automates the model release path without requiring concurrent production versions.

options.name: CI/CD for modular components
pros: Automates component delivery and environment setup.
cons: Component boundaries and failure handling require team ownership.
options.reason: Pairs a dedicated builder with automated delivery and rollback.
